newspaper.teacherDelivery: Open lawful publisher copy, adult reads actual selected short item neutrally (not this paraphrase/model), explain archived UK 2024 context; recheck access and local appropriateness. Child listens and may ask clarification; no independentnewspaperreading prerequisite. Do not call it an Indian local 2026 event or collect private child data.

teachingQuestionsAndKey.question: What were children invited to spot and count?
teachingQuestionsAndKey.key: Birds visiting their playgrounds, according to the selected item.

teachingQuestionsAndKey.question: Which organisation hosted it?
teachingQuestionsAndKey.key: RSPB, as named in the item; explain unfamiliar acronym neutrally if needed.

teachingQuestionsAndKey.question: Is this archived article announcing an activity happening now?
teachingQuestionsAndKey.key: No: the issue and event are dated 2024. The task is listening to an authentic newspaper item, not planning current participation.

freshQuestionsAndKey.question: After hearing the different Gardening Week item, name one activity it describes.
freshQuestionsAndKey.key: For example making a mini pond/garden, pressing flowers or building hedgehog huts; accept accurately attributed example, no practical wildlife handling expected.

freshQuestionsAndKey.question: In which country is the reported event?
freshQuestionsAndKey.key: UK, as explicitly stated; not presumed the pupil’s own community.

source.section: Natural World: Exciting nature events of 2024

television.teacherDelivery: Use actual broadcaster clip with English caption track on actual TV screen atdelivery. Adult checks lawful current access andcaption legibility and device controls first, short sections only, pauses or replays as appropriate. Disable audio for one readingcheck if accessible and suitable so answers actually use subtitles; this is not a hearing/speed/memory test. Audio and physical TV delivery not performed in research. Do not use webpage transcript or our rendered stills as evidence of actual TV subtitle reading.

teachingQuestionsAndKeys.question: Read a title named by one speaker in the first section.
teachingQuestionsAndKeys.key: Accept an accurately read visible title such as Amulet, Bad Guys or Weirdo; unfamiliar titles may be explained, no priorbookknowledge required.

teachingQuestionsAndKeys.question: What does the reporter say Book Week celebrates?
teachingQuestionsAndKeys.key: Books; learner points to/reads the actual relevant subtitle, not only guesses from pictures.

teachingQuestionsAndKeys.question: Does one speaker’s reported reading time tell us how long every child must read?
teachingQuestionsAndKeys.key: No; it is that speaker’s report, not a universal requirement.

freshQuestionsAndKeys.question: Using the new section’s subtitles, name one costume choice.
freshQuestionsAndKeys.key: Inside Out, SpongeBob or Winnie the Pooh, as actually visible in the selected section; no identification of real students required.

freshQuestionsAndKeys.question: What reason does the final speaker give for dressing up?
freshQuestionsAndKeys.key: Expressing the kinds of books they like, according to the selected subtitle; no forced costume or positive attitude expected.
